heroHeadline: Chile Turns Right: Kast Inaugurated, Approval Collapses at 29% as Fuel Protests Grip Nation
heroSubtitle: José Antonio Kast — Chile's most conservative president since Pinochet — took office March 11, 2026 after a 58% runoff victory. Within weeks his approval crashed from 59% to 29% following 32–62% fuel price hikes that triggered the largest cacerolazos since the 2019 estallido. Lithium exports have nearly tripled year-on-year while unions, students, and workers mount sustained resistance.
footerNote: Data sourced from official Chilean government records (Biblioteca del Congreso, Banco Central, SERVEL), Rettig and Valech commissions, IACHR, CIPER Chile, and major international outlets.
